A personal free-tier allowance for clients behind a shared IP (hosted assistants).
Use the returned ``mcp_url`` as the MCP server URL, or send the key as

post.summary: Settle a security deposit after move-out
post.description:
Security deposit settlement for a US rental under the state's statute (and a covered city's ordinance): the date to return the deposit and itemized statement, each intended deduction assessed (allowed or not, prorated by useful life, documentation needed), interest owed, refund due, penalty exposure, a draft itemized statement and a citation for every rule. Covers all 50 states and DC, with city overlays for Chicago, San Francisco, Berkeley, Los Angeles, Seattle, Portland, Minneapolis and Saint Paul.
When to use: A landlord or property manager is closing a move-out and asks when the deposit must be returned, what they may deduct (carpet, paint, cleaning, unpaid rent), how much interest is owed, what to put in the itemized statement, or what happens if they are late.
Not for: Not legal advice and not a tenant demand letter. It does not price repairs (use property_turnover_quick_estimate for that), hold or account for deposits, or cover pet deposits, last-month's rent handling or non-US rentals. Where the statute sets no deadline (Kentucky, Tennessee) it says so; never present a guessed date as the rule.
Tip: Send as_of (today's date) for a repeatable answer; it defaults to today in UTC.
Tip: Give item_installed_on or item_age_years for carpet, paint, blinds and appliances; without them the tenancy length is assumed.
Tip: Mark normal wear with caused_by_tenant false; it is never deductible.
Tip: Relay deadline.return_by and its status, totals.refund_due_usd, penalty_exposure and the citations; say it is not legal advice.
Tip: Offer statement.text as the draft itemized statement; it has no names or addresses.
Tip: Relay warnings, assumptions and unknowns (for example the Texas forwarding address).
Tip: Send the start-event dates a state needs when known (forwarding_address_received_on, demand_received_on, new_tenant_moved_in_on, claim_notice_sent_on in Florida); without them the clock is not_started.
Tip: deadline.status none_in_statute means no statutory deadline; deadline.extended_to is the statute's weekend roll-forward, but advise acting by return_by.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability deposit-settlement v0.1.0 (experimental).

post.summary: Security deposit rules for a state (and city)
post.description:
The security deposit rules for one US state, with a covered city's overlay: return deadline and what starts it, itemization and documentation duties, allowed deductions and depreciation, interest, penalty, deposit cap and recent changes, with citations.
When to use: Someone asks what a state's (or a covered city's) security deposit rules are without a specific move-out to settle, or which states are covered.
Not for: To settle a specific deposit (use deposit_settlement_settle, which applies the rules to the dates and deductions). Other landlord-tenant topics (evictions, rent control, notice periods) are not covered.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability deposit-settlement v0.1.0 (experimental).

The easiest way to estimate a US rental turnover: a ZIP, bedrooms, bathrooms and a list of plain-English issues in, a priced make-ready estimate out (same engine and result as property_turnover_scope, short summary by default).
When to use: Start here when the user describes a move-out or turnover in words ("carpet stained in both bedrooms, oven filthy") and wants a cost estimate or what to tell vendors. Use property_turnover_scope instead for rate cards, owner decisions, measured quantities or per-finding control.
Not for: Diagnosing hazards (they come back as refer-outs to a licensed professional); legal advice on deposits; remodel bids; properties outside the US.
Tip: If the ZIP is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess or pad it.
Tip: Relay refer_outs first, then the totals; say the numbers are estimates, not quotes.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability property-turnover v0.8.0 (experimental).

Turn move-out / turnover inspection findings for a US rental unit into a priced make-ready scope: standardized tasks by trade, regional low/expected/high costs, must/should/could priorities, vendor scopes, refer-outs to licensed professionals, and every assumption stated.
When to use: Turnover findings for a US rental unit when you need control: rooms, measured quantities, the manager's own prices (rate_card) or owner approve/decline decisions. For a plain-English estimate, property_turnover_quick_estimate is easier.
Not for: Diagnosing hazards (they come back as refer-outs to a licensed professional); legal advice on deposits; remodel bids; properties outside the US.
Tip: If the ZIP is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess or pad it.
Tip: Describe each finding in plain words (description). Only send a code returned by property_turnover_issue_codes; unmatched findings come back as manual-quote lines with suggested codes.
Tip: Give measured quantities when you have them (e.g. 120 sq_ft); otherwise typical sizes are assumed and listed in assumptions.
Tip: Send property.floor_coverings when you know whether there is carpet, and unit_type single_family for houses; both change the baseline scope.
Tip: Relay the summary, refer_outs, assumptions and unknowns to the user; costs are estimate ranges, not quotes.
Tip: Use detail=summary unless the user asks for every line item (summary already lists every line tied to a finding).
Tip: Rate card examples - {"trade": "handyman", "unit_price": 65, "uom": "hour"} or {"task_id": "carpet.clean", "unit_price": 0.2, "uom": "sq_ft"}; check rate_card_applied and rate_card_ignored before saying a rate was used.
Tip: For the Excel workbook or owner estimate, give the user links.web_tool_prefilled (opens the free web tool with these findings) or POST the same arguments to links.downloads; do not build a spreadsheet yourself.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability property-turnover v0.8.0 (experimental).

Search the standard taxonomy of rental-unit turnover issues (component.issue codes) by keyword or area.
When to use: Only while preparing findings for a turnover cost estimate, to find the standard issue code for something observed (e.g. "pet stain on carpet"). Never needed to answer a question; call with no arguments to list the taxonomy areas and the first codes.
Not for: Legal or security-deposit questions; anything outside rental turnover and make-ready work. Not needed before quick_estimate or scope: a plain description works there.
Tip: Call with no arguments to list the taxonomy areas (in `areas`) and the first codes.
Tip: Codes are optional for scoping; a plain description also works.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability property-turnover v0.8.0 (experimental).

post.summary: Settle a security deposit after move-out (paid)
post.description: Paid lane (x402 v2, exact scheme, USDC on Base Sepolia testnet, $0.02 per call). Same body as POST /v1/deposit-settlement/settle, which stays free within its rate limits. Unpaid requests get HTTP 402 with PAYMENT-REQUIRED; only successful results are charged. Not available over MCP. The response adds `payment` (network, transaction, payer).

402.description: Payment required (x402 v2). The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header carries the base64 payment requirements; retry with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. Also returned for an invalid payment or a failed settlement (nothing charged).

422.description: Invalid input. Checked before payment; never charged.

429.description: Rate limited (per payer wallet or per client). Never charged.

get.description:
Aggregate settlement counts for the configured network: by payer class and route,
external payers and revenue, and ``qualified_repeat_demand`` (at least 5 external
wallets with at least 5 settled calls each). No wallet addresses; refreshed every few
minutes.

schema.title: Response X402 Metrics V1 X402 Metrics Get

post.summary: Send feedback about the site, a tool, or an idea for a new tool
post.description: Free text plus a scope. For humans (the web forms use it); there is no MCP tool for this on purpose. Messages are capped at 2000 characters, links are replaced with [link] and at most 3 are accepted. Provide an email only if you want a reply. Rate limited to 5 per minute. Leave `website` empty.

Alternative.title: Alternative
Alternative.description:
A different deadline when a condition holds (e.g. 14 days when nothing is deducted).

``condition`` is the statute's case in words. The engine evaluates it when ``requires``
lists mapped conditions, when the condition itself is one (``no_deductions``), or when an
effective-date window is the whole condition; any other alternative keeps the base rule and
adds an assumption naming it. ``combine`` says how a matching alternative applies:
``replace`` the base period (the first match wins), or take the ``later_date`` /
``earlier_date`` of the base deadline and this one (Connecticut: 21 days after the end of
the tenancy or 15 days after the forwarding address, whichever is later).

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: What the citation supports: deadline, interest, penalty, ...

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: Short quote of the rule (or our summary when verbatim is false).

CleaningRule.title: CleaningRule
CleaningRule.description:
How the statute treats a cleaning charge (a line's ``cleaning_kind``: ``beyond_wear``,
``routine`` or unknown).

``basis``: ``named`` when the deposit statute names cleaning as a purpose (to return the unit
to its move-in cleanliness, reasonable cleaning): unknown kind is 'yes' with the limit noted;
``damage`` when it does not, but a unit left dirtier than normal use is recoverable as damage
beyond normal wear, a breach of the tenant's duty to keep it clean, or a lease charge: unknown
kind is 'depends'. ``routine`` (cleaning after ordinary use): ``barred`` ('no': it is normal
wear) or ``lease`` ('depends': only if the lease provides it and the statute lets lease charges
come out of the deposit) or ``reasonable`` ('depends': the statute allows reasonable cleaning
costs with no wear limit, Mississippi, Nevada, Rhode Island, Utah). ``condition``: a precondition (Montana's written notice and 24 hours
to clean), checked against ``documentation.cleaning_notice`` (unknown: 'depends'; no: 'no',
unless ``unless_no_notice`` and the tenant gave no notice of leaving). ``effective_on``: the
version for deductions made on or after this date (Colorado HB25-1249: ordinary uncleanliness
is normal wear from 2026-01-01); the latest in force wins.

ContractDamages.title: ContractDamages
ContractDamages.description:
The statute lets the deposit cover damages from the tenant's noncompliance with the rental
agreement (URLTA wording: Ohio 5321.16(B), Nebraska 76-1416(2), ...), so lease charges it does
not list are 'depends' (the lease, reasonableness, mitigation), never a flat 'no' (round 3
R9: D-OH-06, F-NE-03).

CostRange.title: CostRange
CostRange.description: A low / expected / high estimate. Invariant: low <= expected <= high.

return_by.title: Return By
return_by.description: Last day to return the deposit.

itemization_by.title: Itemization By
itemization_by.description: Last day for the itemized statement (often the same day; earlier in Chicago, later in Louisiana).

extended_to.title: Extended To
extended_to.description: Where the state's code rolls a last day on a weekend or holiday to the next business day: that later date. Act by return_by; this is the legal outer limit.

start_event.title: Start Event
start_event.description: What starts the clock, in words.

days.title: Days
days.description: Period in days (None: months or none).

months.title: Months
months.description: Period in calendar months, if any.

status.title: Status
status.description: upcoming, due_today, overdue; met (the refund and statement went out on time and cover what is owed, per returned) or late (they went out after the last day); not_started when the start event is not given yet; none_in_statute when the statute sets no deadline (Kentucky, Tennessee).

days_remaining.title: Days Remaining
days_remaining.description: Days from as_of to the last day: extended_to when the statute extends a weekend or holiday last day, else return_by (negative when overdue). None once met.

alternatives.title: Alternatives
alternatives.description: Earlier dates that apply on facts not given (send the named input).

DeadlineAlternative.title: DeadlineAlternative
DeadlineAlternative.description:
Another date the rule gives on facts the request does not settle (e.g. Montana's 10 days
if nothing is deducted, when the deductions are not known yet).

Decision.title: Decision
Decision.description: Owner decision. Re-run the same request with decisions to get the approved scope.

category.title: Category
category.description: One of: unpaid_rent, unpaid_utilities, cleaning, carpet, flooring, paint, blinds_window_coverings, appliance, fixture_or_hardware, wall_or_door_repair, key_or_lock, late_fees, lease_break_fee, moving_and_storage, reletting_costs (advertising or a broker to re-rent after an early move-out), trash_and_abandoned_items (removing trash or belongings left behind), other_damage, other. Carpet cleaning is cleaning (with cleaning_kind), not carpet.

description.title: Description
description.description: Your own short note (e.g. 'bedroom carpet, pet stains'). Never stored, hashed or returned; the statement uses the category.

amount_usd.title: Amount Usd
amount_usd.description: Amount you intend to deduct, in dollars (rounded to cents).

item_installed_on.title: Item Installed On
item_installed_on.description: When the item (carpet, paint, appliance...) was installed or last replaced (YYYY-MM-DD). Give this or item_age_years, not both.

item_age_years.title: Item Age Years
item_age_years.description: Age of the item in years at move-out (e.g. 4.5).

useful_life_years.title: Useful Life Years
useful_life_years.description: Override the useful life used for depreciation (years).

caused_by_tenant.title: Caused By Tenant
caused_by_tenant.description: False when the condition is normal wear and tear (never deductible); null when it is disputed or unknown (a tenant checking a landlord's list): the line is then 'depends', with the amount the rule would allow if it is damage.

has_receipt.title: Has Receipt
has_receipt.description: You have a receipt, invoice or estimate for this line.

has_photos.title: Has Photos
has_photos.description: You have photos of this damage.

utility_kind.title: Utility Kind
utility_kind.description: unpaid_utilities only: which utility. Some states allow only some (Massachusetts: water); without it such a line is 'depends'.

late_payments.title: Late Payments
late_payments.description: late_fees only: how many late payments (or months, where the cap is per month) the fee covers. A statutory cap is per late payment; without this, more than one cap is 'depends'.

work_kind.title: Work Kind
work_kind.description: repair (restores the item: never depreciated), replace (a new item: prorated by the old one's remaining life where the rule does), or cleaning (e.g. carpet cleaning: judged as a cleaning line).

rent_through.title: Rent Through
rent_through.description: unpaid_rent only: the last day the rent charged covers. With new_tenant_moved_in_on it decides how much of the rent overlaps the new tenancy (not recoverable: the landlord cannot collect rent twice for the same days).

cleaning_kind.title: Cleaning Kind
cleaning_kind.description: cleaning only: beyond_wear (the unit was left dirtier than normal use; cleaning to restore its move-in condition), routine (ordinary cleaning after normal use, which most states treat as normal wear) or unknown. Where the statute does not name cleaning, an unknown kind is 'depends'.

amount_allowed_usd.title: Amount Allowed Usd
amount_allowed_usd.description: What the rule lets you keep for this line ('depends' lines: not counted in totals until you confirm).

range_low_usd.title: Range Low Usd
range_low_usd.description: A 'depends' line's least amount on the facts given (e.g. rent after a new tenant's rent is credited at the same rate).

exclusive_option.title: Exclusive Option
exclusive_option.description: Part of an either/or the statute sets (an early-termination fee, or the rent and re-renting costs it replaces): the totals count only the larger option.

DepositCap.title: DepositCap
DepositCap.description:
The statutory deposit limit, computed (round 2 class 9).

``effective_on`` / ``effective_by``: the cap applies to deposits collected (``collected``,
California AB 12, Colorado) or leases entered into or renewed (``lease_signed``, Georgia,
Maryland) on or after the date; earlier ones keep ``before_months_rent`` (None: no cap) and
``before_furnished_months``. ``furnished_months``: the cap for a furnished unit (Kansas);
``furnished_exempt``: none for one (Delaware). ``max_rent_usd``: no cap above this rent
(Alaska $2,000). ``min_term_months``: only for leases of at least this term (Delaware: one
year); ``max_term_months``: only for shorter ones (New Mexico: under a year).
``later_months_rent`` from ``later_after_months`` into the tenancy (Pennsylvania: one month
from the second year). ``variant_months``: another limit under facts the request cannot
state (California small landlords 2, Connecticut 62+ 1, North Carolina month-to-month 1.5,
Portland last month's rent 1.5, ...): a deposit between the two is 'depends'.

exceeded.title: Exceeded
exceeded.description: None when it depends on facts not given (see status).

status.title: Status
status.description: within / exceeded the cap; depends: between the cap and another limit that facts not given decide (alternative_cap_usd); unknown: monthly rent missing; no_cap; not_applicable: an exception the inputs show (Alaska rent over $2,000).

alternative_cap_usd.title: Alternative Cap Usd
alternative_cap_usd.description: The other limit when the cap depends on facts not given.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: Other caps by tenancy type or term; checked against the main.

method.title: Method
method.description: straight_line: max(0, 1 - age / useful life); step_table: the band of a published schedule for the item's age (California paint).

age_years.title: Age Years
age_years.description: Age at move-out: full calendar years plus remaining days / 365, 2 decimals.

remaining_fraction.title: Remaining Fraction
remaining_fraction.description: Share of the cost the tenant can be charged, 4 decimals.

source.title: Source
source.description: useful_life row id (row:jurisdiction for a variant) or 'request'.

schedule_source.title: Schedule Source
schedule_source.description: Source id of the step table, when one was used.

range_low_usd.title: Range Low Usd
range_low_usd.description: Where the statute states no formula: the charge under the shortest useful life the sources give (the line is 'depends' at the default-life estimate).

range_high_usd.title: Range High Usd
range_high_usd.description: The same under the longest useful life the sources give.

itemized_statement.title: Itemized Statement
itemized_statement.description: You will send (or sent) an itemized statement.

receipts.title: Receipts
receipts.description: You have receipts or invoices for the repairs and cleaning.

cleaning_notice.title: Cleaning Notice
cleaning_notice.description: You gave the tenant written notice of the cleaning needed and time to do it before charging for cleaning (Montana 70-25-201(3): 24 hours).

move_in_condition_statement.title: Move In Condition Statement
move_in_condition_statement.description: You gave the tenant a written move-in condition statement or checklist (Montana 70-25-206, Washington 59.18.260).

move_out_list.title: Move Out List
move_out_list.description: You inspected the unit and made the move-out damage list in time (Georgia 44-7-33(b): within 3 business days).

due_by.title: Due By
due_by.description: The duty's own last day, if dated.

EstimateContext.title: EstimateContext
EstimateContext.description:
Identifiers of the estimate being rated. Hashes, versions, region and total only.

Every field has a strict format (security review M1): they end up in the feedback digest,
so nothing here may carry free text.

ExcessRemedy.title: ExcessRemedy
ExcessRemedy.description:
A remedy for taking a deposit above the cap (Maryland 8-203(b)(3): up to three times the
extra amount charged, plus fees).

Exclusion.title: Exclusion
Exclusion.description:
A category the statute keeps out of the deposit (Delaware: damage correctable by painting
and ordinary cleaning): 'no', cited.

method.title: Method
method.description: 'ai': read by a language model from free text.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model that read it, e.g. 'gpt-5-nano 2025-08-07'.

Extraction.title: Extraction
Extraction.description:
How a finding was produced, when software read it from free text (contract 0.4.0).

Set by the web tool when its AI reader (Azure OpenAI) turned a person's own words into this
finding. The engine reports such a finding as ``resolution: "ai"`` with ``needs_review``
and flags its lines; it never changes how the finding is priced.

Fallback.title: Fallback
Fallback.description:
A second date for the full refund when the statement is not given in time or none is
needed (Illinois 710/1(a): no statement for property damage within 30 days: the deposit in
full within 45 days of vacating; a rent-only withholding needs no statement). The statement's
own date stays ``itemization_by``.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: site, a specific tool, or an idea for a new tool.

capability.title: Capability
capability.description: Tool id when scope is tool.

page.title: Page
page.description: Path of the page the feedback is about.

email.title: Email
email.description: Only if you want a reply.

FeedbackIn.title: FeedbackIn
FeedbackIn.description: What the site, a tool or an idea box sends to ``POST /v1/feedback``.

id.title: Id
id.description: Your id for this finding; defaults to f1, f2, ... in order.

location.description: Object {"area": "bedroom", "label": "Bedroom 2"}, or a plain string such as "Bedroom 2" or "kitchen" (mapped to an area; other text becomes the label).

code.title: Code
code.description: Optional. Only a code returned by property_turnover_issue_codes (e.g. 'walls.nail_holes'); otherwise leave it out and use description.

description.title: Description
description.description: Plain description if no code, e.g. 'dog urine stains in bedroom carpet'.

extent.description: spot | partial | full; defaults per issue.

quantity.description: Measured amount, e.g. 120 sq_ft. Derived when omitted.

extraction.description: Leave out. Set by the web tool for findings its AI reader produced from free text; they come back as resolution 'ai' with needs_review.

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description: One observed condition. Give a taxonomy `code` if you know it, else a `description`.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: exact: a taxonomy code was given. alias: the description matched an alias. ai: an AI reader chose the code from free text (see confidence, model; needs_review). unmapped: nothing matched (a manual-quote line). not_billed: the description says there is no work ('no mold', 'faucet not leaking', 'fixed by tenant'); no lines, no refer-out; the issue it names is in suggestions and the reason in not_billed_reason.

not_billed_reason.title: Not Billed Reason
not_billed_reason.description: resolution 'not_billed' only. none: says there is none ('no mold', 'mold: none'); ok: says it works or is fine; done: says it was already fixed or done.

text.title: Text
text.description: The finding as given (description, else code), for tracing.

location.title: Location
location.description: Where, as shown on the lines.

match_note.title: Match Note
match_note.description: Set when the match left a fixture word unexplained: check this finding.

uncertain.title: Uncertain
uncertain.description: The description hedges ('mold?', 'maybe', 'possible'). Refer-outs from uncertain findings are check-first: they add a warning instead of holding phases.

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.description: Suggested codes with readable names, best first.

needs_review.title: Needs Review
needs_review.description: True when software read this finding from free text (resolution 'ai'): check it.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: resolution 'ai' only: the AI reader's confidence, 0 to 1.

carpet_present.title: Carpet Present
carpet_present.description: Is there wall-to-wall carpet? Omit if unknown: carpet findings then imply carpet; with no carpet findings, whole-unit carpet cleaning is left out and listed as unknown.

carpet_sq_ft.title: Carpet Sq Ft
carpet_sq_ft.description: Carpeted floor area. Omit to assume 60% of the unit floor area.

FloorCoverings.title: FloorCoverings
FloorCoverings.description: What is on the floors. Drives the carpet-cleaning baseline and whole-unit carpet sizes.

Forfeiture.title: Forfeiture
Forfeiture.description:
A statute's consequence for a missed duty: the landlord loses the right to keep some or
all of the deposit. Computed, not relayed: when the trigger is met as of ``as_of`` (the date
passed and the statement or refund was not sent in time, or a statement sent now would be
late), the barred lines become ``allowed: no`` (``depends`` when ``gate`` needs a finding or
the category is ``contested``) and the totals are recomputed. Before then the lines stand and
a warning names the date. ``not_in_input`` rows turn on facts the request cannot state and
are relayed as unknowns whenever something is deducted.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.description: late_statement, late_return, late_statement_or_return, late_claim_notice or not_in_input (facts the request cannot state).

status.title: Status
status.description: met: the date passed without the statement or refund (or sending it now would be late), so the barred lines are not counted; not_yet: still time; complied: sent on time; not_started: the clock has not started; relieved: the statute excuses the duty here; unknown: turns on facts you did not give.

due_by.title: Due By
due_by.description: The date the duty had to be met by.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: all: every deduction; damage: damage and cleaning only.

gate.title: Gate
gate.description: none, or the finding needed first (bad_faith, ...).

amount_released_usd.title: Amount Released Usd
amount_released_usd.description: What those lines would otherwise have kept from the deposit.

keeps_claim.title: Keeps Claim
keeps_claim.description: The charges can still be sued for separately.

ForfeitureCheck.title: ForfeitureCheck
ForfeitureCheck.description: A statute's forfeiture of the right to withhold, checked against the request.

Guide.title: Guide
Guide.description: An official plain-language resource for the state or city (an agency guide).

required.title: Required
required.description: None: depends on facts you did not give.

rate_percent.title: Rate Percent
rate_percent.description: Percent per year (the move-out rate when rates change).

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: What the rate applies to: deposit, or the excess (Ohio).

base_usd.title: Base Usd
base_usd.description: The amount the rate applies to.

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: Per-period amounts when the rate changed.

if_required_usd.title: If Required Usd
if_required_usd.description: The amount owed if the condition holds (a rent ordinance's interest when coverage is not known); not in the refund.

InterestPart.title: InterestPart
InterestPart.description: One period of an interest computation at one rate (a year, a rate window).

client_refs.title: Client Refs
client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

query.title: Query
query.description: Keywords to match against codes, names and aliases, e.g. 'pet stain carpet'.

area.title: Area
area.description: Optional taxonomy area filter, e.g. 'flooring' or 'walls' (not a room). Call with no arguments to list every area in `areas`.

include_aliases.title: Include Aliases
include_aliases.description: Also return each code's aliases (larger result).

areas.title: Areas
areas.description: Every taxonomy area, for the `area` filter (e.g. 'flooring', 'walls').

city.title: City
city.description: The city you sent, as given.

city_overlay.title: City Overlay
city_overlay.description: The covered city whose rules were layered on, if any.

verified.title: Verified
verified.description: True when the main rule text was read verbatim at the official source and, when a city was given, the city's own rules are covered.

city_rules_checked.title: City Rules Checked
city_rules_checked.description: True: the city's overlay was applied; false: the city you gave is not covered, so only the state rule is shown (a local ordinance may be stricter); null: no city given.

LateFeeRule.title: LateFeeRule
LateFeeRule.description:
The most a late fee may be, per late payment (or per month), computed from the monthly
rent: ``flat_usd`` and ``percent`` (of the rent, or of the rent above ``over_usd``) combined
as the greater, the lesser or the sum; ``rent_tiers`` / ``unit_tiers`` pick the figure by
rent or building size. ``presumption``: the figure is only a safe harbor (Texas), so a larger
fee is 'depends'. ``conditional``: no figure can be checked (Massachusetts: nothing until 30
days late; Oregon's reasonable flat fee; Wisconsin's nonstandard provision): 'depends' with
the text. The engine allows up to the cap for one late payment unless the line says how many
(``late_payments``); more than one cap without a count is 'depends'.

LeaseBreakRule.title: LeaseBreakRule

Location.title: Location
Location.description: Where the finding is. Also accepted as a plain string ("Bedroom 2", "kitchen").

MoveInPhotos.title: MoveInPhotos
MoveInPhotos.description:
Photos at the start of the tenancy, for tenancies beginning on or after ``tenancy_from``
(California 1950.5(g)(1): 2025-07-01). Checked against ``documentation.photos_move_in``.

MoveInStatement.title: MoveInStatement
MoveInStatement.description:
A written move-in condition statement or checklist the statute ties damage deductions to,
checked against ``documentation.move_in_condition_statement`` (Montana 70-25-206(3): without
it, damage and cleaning only on clear and convincing evidence: 'depends'; Washington
59.18.260(5): liable for the whole deposit: ``bars``, ``scope: all``).

MoveOutList.title: MoveOutList
MoveOutList.description:
A move-out inspection and damage list due a number of business days after the tenancy
ends and the tenant vacates (Georgia 44-7-33(b): three business days), checked against
``documentation.move_out_list``; dated, with a due-soon warning.

NotIfAbandoned.title: NotIfAbandoned
NotIfAbandoned.description:
The return rule does not apply when the tenant abandons (Louisiana 9:3251(C)): decided by
``tenant_abandoned`` (else no proper notice or a move-out before the end of the tenancy).

refund_min_usd.title: Refund Min Usd
refund_min_usd.description: The refund if every 'depends' line is kept.

interest_usd.title: Interest Usd
interest_usd.description: Interest owed and computed; None when interest is owed but not computed (see interest_unknown) or not owed.

interest_unknown.title: Interest Unknown
interest_unknown.description: Interest is (or may be) owed but its amount is not computed.

returned_usd.title: Returned Usd
returned_usd.description: Already returned to the tenant (returned.amount_usd; the deposit for a full refund with no amount; 0 for nothing); None when not said or not given.

owed_now_usd.title: Owed Now Usd
owed_now_usd.description: Still owed to the tenant: refund_due_usd minus returned_usd, never below 0 (None when the amount returned is not known).

next_due.title: Next Due
next_due.description: The earliest open step's last day (what to act on first).

uncertain.title: Uncertain
uncertain.description: What the answer still turns on, in words.

Outcome.title: Outcome
Outcome.description:
The one answer every other section is worded from: what is owed to the tenant now, by
when, and what is still uncertain.

in_addition_to_refund.title: In Addition To Refund
in_addition_to_refund.description: The damages come on top of returning the amount withheld (Ohio, West Virginia), not instead of it.

estimated_min_usd.title: Estimated Min Usd
estimated_min_usd.description: The least of the readings when the statute's base is unsettled (a refund paid late, 'depends' lines, IL's 'deposit due'); None when it is the same as the max.

base.title: Base
base.description: What a multiple of the amount withheld is taken of: withheld, wrongfully_withheld, entitled_balance or exceeds_damages.

estimated_max_usd.title: Estimated Max Usd
estimated_max_usd.description: fixed + multiple x basis amount (with any floor or cap); exposure, not a verdict. None when the basis is unknown (monthly rent not given).

forfeits_right_to_withhold.title: Forfeits Right To Withhold
forfeits_right_to_withhold.description: True: a late statement or refund takes away the right to withhold with no court finding; None: it does only on a finding (bad faith, willful, unreasonable); False: the statute states no such forfeiture.

additional.title: Additional
additional.description: City penalties in addition to the state's (not included in its estimate).

forfeits_right_to_withhold_if_late.title: Forfeits Right To Withhold If Late

Phase.title: Phase
Phase.description: Make-ready order. Values sort in sequence order via PHASE_ORDER.

PriceTier.title: PriceTier
PriceTier.description: Purchasing channel. Library prices are pm_vendor (a PM buying turns from a local vendor).

unit_type.description: Single-family homes and townhomes get house-sized defaults (floor area, locks).

client_refs.title: Client Refs
client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

zip.title: Zip
zip.description: The user's 5-digit US ZIP code. If it is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess, pad or correct it.

issues.title: Issues
issues.description: What was found in plain English, e.g. ['stained carpet in both bedrooms', 'nail holes everywhere', 'oven is filthy']. Read like pasted notes: an entry may hold several conditions ('carpet stained, nail holes'; one finding each); a room before or after the condition sets the location ('Bedroom 2 carpet torn', 'mold in bathroom'); a written count sets the quantity ('3 blinds broken'); an entry saying there is no work ('no mold', 'leak fixed by tenant') is reported as not billed.

QuickEstimateRequest.title: QuickEstimateRequest
QuickEstimateRequest.description: Flat, primitive-only input: the easiest way to get an estimate.

task_id.title: Task Id
task_id.description: A task_id from a result line, e.g. 'carpet.clean'.

unit_price.title: Unit Price
unit_price.description: USD per uom. On a trade entry, uom 'hour' is an hourly labor rate (replaces the labor part of that trade's prices); another uom prices that trade's tasks in it.

uom.description: Unit your price is quoted in. Required with a trade unit_price. If it differs from a task's uom, the entry is not applied to that task (see rate_card_ignored).

RateCardEntry.title: RateCardEntry
RateCardEntry.description:
Your own price. Examples: {"trade": "handyman", "unit_price": 65, "uom": "hour"} (an
hourly labor rate for that trade); {"trade": "painter", "min_charge": 150} (visit minimum);
{"task_id": "carpet.clean", "unit_price": 0.2, "uom": "sq_ft"} (task_id from a result line).
A task_id entry beats a trade entry; both beat the library. The result lists what was
applied and what was ignored (rate_card_applied / rate_card_ignored).

RateWindow.title: RateWindow
RateWindow.description:
A published rate for a period (San Francisco's March-February year, a Berkeley move-out
month, a Connecticut calendar year).

unconfirmed.title: Unconfirmed
unconfirmed.description: Every triggering finding was hedged ('maybe', '?'): check first; no phase is held until the condition is confirmed (see warnings).

RentTier.title: RentTier
RentTier.description: A flat late-fee limit for rents up to ``max_rent_usd`` (Iowa: $60 a month up to $700).

what.title: What
what.description: nothing: nothing returned yet; full_refund: the whole deposit; partial_refund: part of it, with no itemized statement; itemized_statement: an itemized statement of deductions (with any refund the same day).

on.title: On
on.description: Day it was sent or delivered (YYYY-MM-DD); required unless what is nothing. Statutes count the day the landlord mails or delivers it; a postmark is the best evidence.

Returned.title: Returned
Returned.description:
What the landlord has returned so far: lets the result say whether the refund and the
itemized statement came on time (``timeliness``).

covered_cities.title: Covered Cities
covered_cities.description: City overlays in this state ('Name, ST').

guides.title: Guides
guides.description: Official plain-language guides for this state or city, where we have one.

small_claims.description: The state courts' small claims page, where we have one.

research_notes.title: Research Notes
research_notes.description: Research notes on the rows used: where the text was read, fetch failures, renumbering, history not checked. For checking the sourcing; not warnings.

SafeHarbor.title: SafeHarbor
SafeHarbor.description:
What takes the penalty away (Illinois 710/1(a), Pennsylvania 512(e), Ohio 5321.16(B), ...):
the tenant gave no forwarding address. Checked against ``tenant_gave_forwarding_address``
(false: no penalty; unknown with no address received: an unknown says so).

responsibility_by_finding.title: Responsibility By Finding
responsibility_by_finding.description: Set when the hint is 'mixed': the hint of each finding the line carries.

allowance.description: Quote-required lines only: a non-binding budget range. NOT included in any total; summed separately in totals.allowances.

to_confirm.title: To Confirm
to_confirm.description: Every finding behind this line is uncertain, or it is a check-first assessment from the safety net: priced, but not in must/should/could, subtotal or total (see totals.to_confirm).

needs_review.title: Needs Review
needs_review.description: A finding behind this line was read by AI from free text: check it.

client_refs.title: Client Refs
client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

retain.title: Retain
retain.description: Optional (contract 0.5.0). false: keep none of this request's text. By default the finding descriptions are kept with contact details and access codes removed, to improve matching; the estimate is the same either way.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: summary: totals, trade scopes, every line tied to a finding (capped at 40) plus the largest must-fix/refer-out lines, a one-line note on the routine lines left out, notes, and only findings needing attention (small). full: every line, finding and source.

lines_omitted.title: Lines Omitted
lines_omitted.description: Lines left out in summary detail.

omitted_note.title: Omitted Note
omitted_note.description: Summary detail: what the omitted lines are (routine turn tasks) and their cost.

rate_card_applied.title: Rate Card Applied
rate_card_applied.description: Rate card entries that changed a price.

rate_card_ignored.title: Rate Card Ignored
rate_card_ignored.description: Rate card entries that changed nothing, with why.

ScopeResult.title: ScopeResult
ScopeResult.description:
Field order puts the answer first (summary, disclaimer, totals, refer-outs, vendor
scopes), because agents and truncating clients read from the top.

client_refs.title: Client Refs
client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

state.title: State
state.description: US state, 2-letter code (e.g. 'CA'); a state name also works.

city.title: City
city.description: City, for a city overlay where covered (e.g. 'Chicago'). Optional.

monthly_rent_usd.title: Monthly Rent Usd
monthly_rent_usd.description: Monthly rent, for the deposit cap check.

building_units.title: Building Units
building_units.description: Units in the building. Some interest rules depend on it (NY 6+, IL 25+).

move_in_on.title: Move In On
move_in_on.description: Tenancy start (YYYY-MM-DD). Used for interest and, when an item's age is unknown, for depreciation.

tenancy_ended_on.title: Tenancy Ended On
tenancy_ended_on.description: Lease end or termination date (YYYY-MM-DD), if different.

vacated_on.title: Vacated On
vacated_on.description: Day the tenant moved out and returned possession (YYYY-MM-DD).

forwarding_address_received_on.title: Forwarding Address Received On
forwarding_address_received_on.description: Day you received the tenant's written forwarding address (YYYY-MM-DD). Several states start or hold the clock on it (Texas, Connecticut, Iowa, Minnesota).

tenant_gave_forwarding_address.title: Tenant Gave Forwarding Address
tenant_gave_forwarding_address.description: False when the tenant never gave a forwarding address in writing (not just 'not yet known'). Illinois, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Delaware, South Carolina and New Hampshire then relieve the landlord of the penalty. Implied true by forwarding_address_received_on.

demand_received_on.title: Demand Received On
demand_received_on.description: Day you received the tenant's written demand for the deposit (YYYY-MM-DD). Arizona, Kansas, Oklahoma, South Carolina and Mississippi start the clock on it.

new_tenant_moved_in_on.title: New Tenant Moved In On
new_tenant_moved_in_on.description: Day a new tenant moved in, if the unit was re-rented (YYYY-MM-DD). West Virginia and Wisconsin can end the period earlier; rent claimed for days from it on is not recoverable (re-rent mitigation).

new_tenant_rent_usd.title: New Tenant Rent Usd
new_tenant_rent_usd.description: Monthly rent the new tenant pays (with new_tenant_moved_in_on): the rent received for overlapping days is credited against rent claimed for them.

statement_sent_on.title: Statement Sent On
statement_sent_on.description: Day you sent (or delivered) the itemized statement (YYYY-MM-DD). With it the statement is judged on time or late; documentation.itemized_statement alone cannot tell.

claim_notice_sent_on.title: Claim Notice Sent On
claim_notice_sent_on.description: Day you sent the written notice of intent to impose a claim on the deposit (YYYY-MM-DD). Florida (due within 30 days of termination) and the District of Columbia (within 45 days): the balance is due 30 days after it; a late notice does not count.

lease_return_days.title: Lease Return Days
lease_return_days.description: Return period the lease sets, in days, where the statute lets a lease set one (Colorado up to 60, Idaho up to 30, Maine shorter).

tenant_gave_proper_notice.title: Tenant Gave Proper Notice
tenant_gave_proper_notice.description: A termination notice that meets the statute was given (Alaska: 14 days instead of 30 when nothing is deducted for damage).

interest_paid_through.title: Interest Paid Through
interest_paid_through.description: Interest already paid or credited to the tenant up to this day (annual-payment rules: San Francisco, Los Angeles, Berkeley, Connecticut, Massachusetts, ...): interest is counted from it.

nonstandard_provision_signed.title: Nonstandard Provision Signed
nonstandard_provision_signed.description: Wisconsin: the tenant signed a separate NONSTANDARD RENTAL PROVISIONS document covering the charge (ATCP 134.06(3)(b)); false makes such charges 'no'.

pet_deposit_usd.title: Pet Deposit Usd
pet_deposit_usd.description: The part of deposit_usd that is a pet deposit (outside the cap in Missouri, Alabama, North Dakota).

tenant_age_62_plus.title: Tenant Age 62 Plus
tenant_age_62_plus.description: The tenant is 62 or older (Connecticut: a one-month cap).

small_landlord.title: Small Landlord
small_landlord.description: California AB 12 small landlord (a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning at most two properties with at most four units; not for a service member): a two-month cap.

owner_occupied.title: Owner Occupied
owner_occupied.description: The landlord lives in the building (ME, NH, NJ and Chicago exempt small owner-occupied buildings; with building_units).

landlord_units_owned.title: Landlord Units Owned
landlord_units_owned.description: Rental units the landlord owns in all (Arkansas 5 or fewer, Georgia 10 or fewer, with third_party_managed, may be exempt).

third_party_managed.title: Third Party Managed
third_party_managed.description: A third party manages the unit or collects rent for a fee.

prepaid_rent_usd.title: Prepaid Rent Usd
prepaid_rent_usd.description: Rent paid in advance beyond the first month, held besides deposit_usd (Connecticut counts it toward the cap).

tenancy_type.title: Tenancy Type
tenancy_type.description: written_lease or at_will (Maine 6033(2): a written agreement's period, at most 30 days, or 21 days for a tenancy at will).

tenant_abandoned.title: Tenant Abandoned
tenant_abandoned.description: The tenant abandoned the unit or was evicted (Maryland 8-203(h): the clock runs from the tenant's written demand; Louisiana 9:3251(C): the one-month rule does not apply). Left out: inferred from tenant_gave_proper_notice: false or a move-out before tenancy_ended_on.

contractor_needed.title: Contractor Needed
contractor_needed.description: Damage exceeds the deposit and needs a third-party contractor, and you said so in writing in time (Virginia, West Virginia: 15 more days).

deposit_collected_on.title: Deposit Collected On
deposit_collected_on.description: Day the deposit was collected (YYYY-MM-DD); defaults to move_in_on. California (AB 12, from 2024-07-01) and Colorado caps depend on it.

lease_signed_or_renewed_on.title: Lease Signed Or Renewed On
lease_signed_or_renewed_on.description: Day the current lease was signed or last renewed (YYYY-MM-DD). Georgia (2024-07-01) and Maryland (2024-10-01) caps apply to leases from then; defaults to move_in_on, with a warning that a later renewal may bring the new cap.

lease_term_months.title: Lease Term Months
lease_term_months.description: Term of the lease in months (0 for month-to-month). Delaware's cap applies to leases of a year or more, New Mexico's to shorter ones.

furnished.title: Furnished
furnished.description: The unit is rented furnished (California before AB 12: 3 months; Kansas: 1.5 months; Delaware: no cap).

rent_ordinance_covered.title: Rent Ordinance Covered
rent_ordinance_covered.description: The unit is covered by the city's rent ordinance (Los Angeles RSO, Berkeley Rent Ordinance). Their deposit interest is owed only then; unknown: the amount is shown beside the refund, not in it.

interest_rate_percent.title: Interest Rate Percent
interest_rate_percent.description: Annual rate the deposit account paid, where the law sets interest at the bank's rate (New Jersey, North Dakota, Illinois 765 ILCS 715, Portland). Without it that interest is unknown.

deductions.title: Deductions
deductions.description: What you intend to deduct (or, for a tenant, what the landlord listed). An explicit empty list means nothing is deducted (it decides the shorter no-deduction periods, e.g. Montana 10 days, Alaska 14); leave it out when that is not known yet.

returned.description: What the landlord has returned so far and when. With it, timeliness says whether the refund and the itemized statement were on time and how many days late.

documentation.description: What documentation you have; leave a field out when unknown.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: Today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the deadline status. Defaults to today (UTC); send it for repeatable results.

forfeiture.title: Forfeiture
forfeiture.description: The statute's forfeitures of the right to withhold, checked; a met one has already taken its lines out of the totals.

outcome.description: What is owed to the tenant now, by when, and what is uncertain: the summary, deadline status and statement are worded from it.

timeliness.description: Present when the request says what was returned (returned).

guides.title: Guides
guides.description: Official plain-language guides for this state or city, where we have one.

small_claims.description: The state courts' small claims page, where we have one.

duty.title: Duty
duty.description: itemized_statement (or notice of claim, where it has its own date), refund (the deposit or the balance), or interest still unpaid after the refund.

due_by.title: Due By
due_by.description: The last day, with the statute's roll-forward applied.

days.title: Days
days.description: Days left (upcoming), or days late (late, overdue, short).

Stage.title: Stage
Stage.description: One dated step of the rule, as it stands on as_of.

price_tier.description: bulk_contract (portfolio contract prices) | pm_vendor (default: a property manager buying turns from local vendors) | retail_one_off (an owner hiring one contractor).

markup_pct.title: Markup Pct
markup_pct.description: Management markup applied to every line, %.

text.title: Text
text.description: Draft itemized statement, plain text, no names or addresses.

late.title: Late
late.description: True: a duty is late or overdue (with nothing returned: every way the rule can be met has passed). False: on time or not yet due. None: no deadline, or the clock has not started.

days_late.title: Days Late
days_late.description: Days late (the most of any duty; with nothing returned, the days since the last way of meeting the rule passed).

late_since.title: Late Since
late_since.description: With nothing returned: the day from which it is late.

amount_kept_usd.title: Amount Kept Usd
amount_kept_usd.description: Deposit minus the amount returned (what is withheld).

difference_usd.title: Difference Usd
difference_usd.description: totals.refund_due_usd minus the amount returned (positive: less came back than the rule's refund on the deductions given).

Timeliness.title: Timeliness
Timeliness.description: Whether what the landlord returned (``returned``) came on time.

due_by.title: Due By
due_by.description: Last day under the rule, with the statute's weekend or holiday roll-forward applied (the legal limit).

done_on.title: Done On
done_on.description: When it was sent; None: not yet.

status.title: Status
status.description: on_time / late (done, by or after due_by); not_yet_due / overdue (not done as of as_of); not_started (the start event is missing); none_in_statute.

days_late.title: Days Late
days_late.description: Days after due_by (late, or overdue as of as_of).

TimelyCheck.title: TimelyCheck
TimelyCheck.description: One duty checked against its deadline: the refund, or the itemized statement.

UnitTier.title: UnitTier
UnitTier.description: A percentage for buildings up to ``max_units`` (Texas: 12% up to four units).

UtilityLimit.title: UtilityLimit
UtilityLimit.description:
Utility charges the statute lets the landlord deduct, by kind (Massachusetts: water only).
A utility line is 'yes' for these kinds, 'no' for others, 'depends' when the kind is not
given (``utility_kind`` on the line).

allowed_usd.title: Allowed Usd
allowed_usd.description: Sum of lines with allowed = yes.

depends_usd.title: Depends Usd
depends_usd.description: Sum of 'depends' lines at the amount the rule would allow if they stand (not in allowed_usd or the refund).

interest_usd.title: Interest Usd
interest_usd.description: Interest credited (0 when none or unknown).

tenant_owes_usd.title: Tenant Owes Usd
tenant_owes_usd.description: Allowed deductions above deposit + interest (collect separately).

refund_min_usd.title: Refund Min Usd
refund_min_usd.description: The refund if every 'depends' line stands: deposit + interest - allowed - depends, never below 0. Equals refund_due_usd when nothing depends.

note.title: Note
note.default: must, should and could are work lines only. visit_charges (minimum call-out and trip fees, once per trade) are added on top: subtotal = must + should + could + visit_charges; total = subtotal + tax. allowances and to_confirm (uncertain items) are outside the total.

to_confirm.description: Lines from uncertain findings ('maybe', '?', 'possible') and safety items read from plain words (the refer-out safety net): priced, but outside every total until confirmed on site. Those lines carry to_confirm: true (contract 0.7.0).

allowances.description: Budget allowance for quote-required lines (refer-outs, manual quotes). Shown outside the totals: subtotal and total never include it.
